scenario: Balloon-borne cosmic-ray detectors only log flux measurements exceeding 90 counts/min (hardware trigger threshold). Logged values show a mean of 145 counts/min (σ=30 counts/min). Physicists want the true mean cosmic-ray flux at balloon altitude.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming cosmic-ray flux follows a normal distribution with σ=30 counts/min, solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 90] = 145. (b) What fraction of all cosmic-ray flux events lie above the 90 counts/min threshold? (c) By how much (in counts/min) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 145 counts/min is E[X|X>90], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=145 numerically yields μ=142.26451 counts/min. Only 95.9% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 2.73549 counts/min. Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean cosmic-ray flux is 145 counts/min because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 90 counts/min are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>90], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=90, σ=30. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 145 and solve for μ via brentq on [-660.0, 144.9999]. (4) Solution: μ=142.26451 counts/min. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((90−142.26451)/30)=0.95926.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 145,30,90
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-142.26451)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.95926)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-2.73549)<0.01
